data.text:
Approve gated command 'claim.force' for agent close-blshared?  [request Qe744f44816]
  command : ddflow claim <id> --approval request|ID
  item    : B189    target: -
  acts on : the item and who holds its lease (or that it is in review)
  digest  : 3dac2fdd0398800c  (the state is read again when the agent runs it)
  needs   : tier T2, assurance level L1 or stronger; 1 use(s)
  agent's reason (untrusted, not part of the approval): ""

data.summary: B189 (the only open task of BL-shared-log) is 'not ready: phase P-docs-generic/P-roadmap/P-docs-search have open tasks (inherited from BL-shared-log)'. The phase's needs exist for the phase's own close, but a task that the phase waits on inherits them, so closing the phase needs a forced claim approval for its last task. Expected: a task inherits needs only when it declares none AND they are not phase-closing dependencies, or claim treats phase-level needs as gating the phase, not its tasks.
data.title: A phase's own open task inherits the phase's needs, so it cannot be claimed without claim.force

chunk_findings.detail: `_on_a_remote` only treats a lease branch as published when `refs/remotes/<remote>/<same branch name>` contains its tip. It never looks at any other remote ref (for example `origin/main` after a merge) and never asks the remote. Given lease branch `ddflow/T1` with 2 commits that were merged and pushed to `origin/main`, and no `refs/remotes/origin/ddflow/T1`, `unpushed` still returns that row and `block` says those commits are held by no remote and a fresh clone would miss the work. A clone of `main` already has them, so the warning is false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/unpushed.py:31

chunk_findings.detail: `_own_commits` turns any failed `rev-list` into 0, and `unpushed` then skips the item (`if own`). Given `it.base` set to a missing SHA (GC'd or renamed base) and `ddflow/<id>` existing with commits absent from every remote-tracking ref, the count is 0, the brief stays empty, and leased work that a clone would not have is not reported.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/unpushed.py:25

chunk_findings.detail: <ddflow/services/unpushed.py:30: `_own_commits` calls `rev-list --count {base}..{branch}`. If `base` is not an ancestor of `branch` (for instance, when `base` has diverged or is an unrelated history), `rev-list` prints an error or count that does not represent the actual commits unique to the branch, causing incorrect unpushed counts or command failure when evaluated on a non-linear branch history.>
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/unpushed.py:30

chunk_findings.detail: `_own_commits` turns any `rev-list` failure into 0, and `unpushed` only warns when that count is non-zero. Given a live lease whose `it.base` (or `base_ref`) is not a resolvable revision in this clone, `git rev-list --count <base>..<branch>` exits non-zero, the function returns 0, and `block` emits `""` even though `ddflow/<id>` has commits no remote-tracking ref contains. The safety notice fails open.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/unpushed.py:25

chunk_findings.detail: `_on_a_remote` only asks whether `refs/remotes/<remote>/<same branch name>` contains the tip. Given `origin` present, lease branch `ddflow/T1` with one commit that was merged to `main` and pushed so `refs/remotes/origin/main` contains that commit, and no `refs/remotes/origin/ddflow/T1`, `unpushed` still returns the row and `block` says that commit is one "no remote holds", which is false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/unpushed.py:31

chunk_findings.detail: `git rev-list --count <branch> --not --remotes <base>` passes `base` as a bare argument, so Git treats it as ambiguous when that name is both a revision and a worktree path. The preceding check uses `base^{commit}`, which is unambiguously a revision, so a branch named `main` still passes the guard; the count then dies with `fatal: ambiguous argument 'main': both revision and filename` and the `else 0` path returns 0. Given a live lease on `ddflow/T1` with one commit no remote contains, `it.base` unset, `worktree.base_ref` (or the unresolvable-base fallback `default_branch`) equal to `main`, and a file named `main` in the repo, `unpushed` drops the row and brief stays silent even though a fresh clone cannot get that commit. The old `base..branch` form could not be a pathspec; this command line can.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/unpushed.py:31
